content: The reticuloendothelial system (RES), a component of the immune system, is composed of phagocytic cells found in reticular connective tissue. These cells primarily include monocytes and macrophages. They are concentrated in lymph nodes and the spleen. Kupffer cells in the liver and tissue histiocytes are also integral parts of the RES. The terms mononuclear phagocytic system and lymphoreticular system are synonymous with the RES. This system is categorized into primary and secondary lymphoid organs. Primary lymphoid organs are the sites where the cells of the RES are generated. These cells are produced in the bone marrow. The thymus is also considered a primary lymphoid organ because it is essential for the maturation of T cells. Secondary lymphoid organs are the sites where the cells of the RES perform their functions. These include the lymph nodes, spleen, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT). MALT is further subdivided into gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) and bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (BALT). Kupffer cells in the liver also contribute to this system, although they are not organized into a specific tissue structure; instead, they are dispersed throughout the liver sinusoids. The secondary lymphoid structures are responsible for monitoring all incoming or circulating antigens and initiating an immune response against foreign antigens upon their detection. GALT and BALT are specialized to handle the numerous antigens entering the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts, respectively. All extracellular fluid must pass through lymph nodes as it travels through the lymphatic system on its way back to systemic circulation. Antigens present in the interstitial fluid are thus transported to the lymph nodes for processing. The spleen, on the other hand, filters the blood to identify antigens. When foreign antigens are detected, all these tissues respond in a coordinated manner to mount a robust and multifaceted immune response. Clinically, the reticuloendothelial system is significant in certain conditions. In patients with haemochromatosis, the RES serves as a site for iron accumulation. Additionally, lymphoma involving the reticuloendothelial system is referred to as reticuloendotheliosis.
